prompt: explain how a bank run happens and why it can bring down a healthy bank

keyLinks.cause: Banks lend out or invest most deposits
keyLinks.effect: Only a small part of deposits is available as cash at any moment
keyLinks.mechanism: Deposits can be withdrawn any time, but loans and investments pay back slowly

keyLinks.cause: A rumour or bad news spreads
keyLinks.effect: Some depositors fear losing their money and withdraw
keyLinks.mechanism: Whoever withdraws first is more likely to get paid in full

keyLinks.cause: Withdrawals exceed the cash on hand
keyLinks.effect: The bank must sell assets quickly, often at a loss
keyLinks.mechanism: Long-term assets can't be turned into cash fast without discounts

keyLinks.effect: More depositors panic and withdraw (reinforcing loop)
keyLinks.mechanism: Each withdrawal makes it more likely the bank runs out, so waiting looks riskier

keyLinks.cause: The bank runs out of cash
keyLinks.effect: It can't pay depositors and fails, even if it was sound before
keyLinks.mechanism: A liquidity shortage, not initial insolvency, is enough to bring it down

keyLinks.cause: Deposit insurance or central bank lending
keyLinks.effect: Depositors don't need to rush, which stops the loop
keyLinks.mechanism: If money is guaranteed, being first no longer matters

knownErrors.claim: Bank runs only happen to banks that have already lost the money / are insolvent
knownErrors.why: Runs can bring down solvent banks through lack of cash

knownErrors.claim: Banks keep all deposits in the vault
knownErrors.why: Most deposits are lent out or invested

knownErrors.claim: Withdrawals destroy money or make it disappear
knownErrors.why: The money moves to depositors; the bank's problem is running out of cash

knownErrors.claim: The panic loop is balancing / calms itself
knownErrors.why: Each withdrawal increases fear and further withdrawals: it is reinforcing

acceptableSimplifications: Talking about "cash in the vault" instead of reserves
Omitting interbank markets and regulation details
Using a single bank as the whole story
